messages.subject: pseudomarker names - locxx value explanation?
parts:
Karl & R/qtl user group:

 

For background, see my below summary output, which generated scanone  pos and  lod  values for each of the 20 soybean chromosomes.  Also listed in that output, is the corresponding (nearest) genetic marker (i.e., Sxxxxx), OR pseudomarker (i.e., cx.locxx).  Note that I used a step=2 specification in the calc.genoprob cmd.    

 

1st Question:  How is the xx value in the cx. locxx name of the  pseudomarker determined, and why is the locxx number so different from the corresponding column pos value?    Example in particular:   c10.loc42   10  56.26  1.955    The listed genetic markers do have map positions very close to their corresponding pos values.  I could not find any explanation in the R/qtl manual about this locxx question. 

 

2nd Question:  For convenience, can the summary data be output with marker names only (instead of both marker and psuedomarker names)?  I also used the find.marker and find.pseudomarker cmds to find the closest of these to the summary output positions (see below), and note that the following two markers have positions close to the pseudomarker pos=56.26 :

Chr 10 markers: “S17019” pos=54.375 & “S13582” pos=58.489

 

Request:  I lack experience in R, so if anyone could offer some R coding that would take all 20 lod score values in the below summary output and automatically calculate the corresponding R2 values, I would greatly appreciate getting that code.  I currently do the R2 calculation manually (see below) for a given map population, but I like to use a common R/qtl text batchfile for multiple map populations, so it would be quite handy to just have all 20 R2 values automatically generated (even if most are superfluous).  I could then simply examine the 20-chr R2 list to get the R2 ones corresponding to the significant putative QTLs.    

 

Jim

 

-----------------------------------------------

OBJNAME <- calc.genoprob(OBJNAME, map.function=c("kosambi"), step=2, error.prob=0.001)

summary(OBJNAME, threshold=3, df=TRUE)
